title: Why did the capital move to Rio in 1763?
hook: Gold from Minas Gerais needed a way to the sea, and the way ran through Rio.
summary: Gold from Minas Gerais made Rio’s port the colony’s link to Europe, and in 1763 the capital moved there.

cardBlocks.text: In the early 1700s, the discovery of gold and gemstones in Minas Gerais shifted the colony’s centre of gravity. The riches had to reach Europe, and Rio de Janeiro became the key outlet: the main link between the mining interior and the far side of the Atlantic.

That importance led to the move. In 1763, the Marquis of Pombal, King Joseph I’s minister, transferred the capital from Salvador to Rio. The main aim was tighter control over the gold leaving Brazil, but the move also helped defend Portuguese interests in the south of the colony. Rio became the seat of government and the viceroys’ residence.
Gold from Minas Gerais left through Rio’s port; in 1763 the capital moved there to control that flow.

deepDiveBlocks.text: From 1763, every governor of Brazil was given the title of viceroy. The post ended in 1808, when the Portuguese court arrived and began ruling directly from Rio.
With the gold and its new role as capital, Rio became the colony’s main centre. It was also one of the main ports of Atlantic trade, including the trade in enslaved Africans.
